sermon.title: The Mystery of Christ and the Church
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Starting from Ephesians 5:31–32, Pastor David G. Kincer shows that marriage is a parable of Christ and the church, then traces parables of Christ through Genesis—Creator (1:26), Judge at Babel (11:7), Conqueror of Satan (3:15), the Lamb (3:21), and the ark as the church (6:18)—confirmed in the New Testament. He closes with prophecy fulfilled as proof only the God of the Bible predicts the future.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Two words were not clear (9:50, 20:30). Sensitive content kept as spoken: a crude hot-dog illustration of sex in marriage versus homosexual couples (0:50); his teaching that all races (including skin color) came from Babel, which goes beyond the text of Genesis 11; the resurrected body having no blood; Islam/Muhammad and Buddha. He says “John chapter 9 and 10” for “I am the door” (John 10:9) and briefly says “Galatians” before correcting to Genesis.

faqs.question: Does God honor marriages outside the church?
faqs.answer: Yes—whether by justice of the peace, minister, or at home, once you commit and say the vow God honors everybody’s marriage, not just Christians.

faqs.question: Are the Father, Son and Spirit separate gods?
faqs.answer: No—he says when you talk about God you are talking about Jesus and the Holy Spirit; they are all one.

faqs.question: Where did the races come from?
faqs.answer: He says at Babel Jesus changed their language and body makeup and all the races come from that event.

faqs.question: Should Christians argue with Satan?
faqs.answer: No—don’t talk with Satan; go to his leader Jesus and ask him to take care of it.

faqs.question: Did God die on the cross?
faqs.answer: He says God can’t die; the fleshly body Jesus lived in died, just as our flesh dies but our spirit continues living.

faqs.question: What does Emmanuel mean?
faqs.answer: God with us—God himself was in the body of Christ.

faqs.question: Will our resurrected bodies have blood?
faqs.answer: He says Christ’s risen body had no blood, and our immortal bodies will be kept alive by God himself.

faqs.question: Why keep coming to church?
faqs.answer: He says the presence of Jesus in the church kept drawing him back, because Jesus promised to be there when we gather.

faqs.question: Can we understand the Bible without the Holy Spirit?
faqs.answer: Spiritual things are discerned by the Spirit; you need the Holy Ghost opening your understanding.

faqs.question: Is preaching Jesus as the only way hate speech?
faqs.answer: No—it is love speech, because God cares for the condition of mankind.
